diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑api latency spiked after the 10:15 pm deployment of v4.17, reaching a p95 of 2 150 ms. The spike is caused by an exhausted database connection pool that was reduced from 50 to 10 connections.
diagnosis.root_cause: The checkout-api release changed orders-db pool settings to max_connections=10 and acquire_timeout_ms=2000, causing ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and long db.pool.acquire spans.

evidence.finding: p95 latency jumped from 200 ms to 2 150 ms within minutes of the deployment
orders-db pool had max_connections=10, in_use=10, waiting=143 and acquire_timeouts_per_min=212 at 10:40
Error logs show ConnectionPoolTimeoutError with 2000 ms timeout and 212 occurrences in the last 15 min
Slow trace shows db.pool.acquire span of 1 829 ms, matching the pool timeout
Diff reveals config/database.yaml changed max_connections from 50 to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms from 5000 to 2000

ruled_out: Other services deployments (payment-gateway, inventory-api) – their versions did not change and latency remained normal

proposal.rationale: The latency spike is caused by the checkout‑api v4.17 deployment reducing the orders-db connection pool to 10 connections, leading to ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and long db.pool.acquire spans. Rolling back to the previous stable release (v4.16) restores the original pool settings and resolves the issue.
